messages:
nina: quick brain-dump — i hacked together an alternate scoring approach for the dedicated-pool autoscaler: instead of instant token drains on admission, amortize token consumption across a lease window so short bursts don't immediately spike eviction. posting prototype math & tradeoffs below.

 tom: sounds promising. can you summarize the amortization rule in one sentence?

 nina: sure: when a request consumes X tokens, we charge X / lease_ttl per second to the tenant's token-balance gauge rather than subtracting X upfront. that way a 30s short job only creates a small immediate delta and spreads the accounting.

 elaine: interesting. how do you handle concurrent short requests? if lots of short jobs start at once we might still oversubscribe.

 nina: good point. we keep a short-window spike detector: if instantaneous inflight_tokens > peak_threshold, we escalate admission to consult operator absolute headroom (fallback). otherwise amortization applies.

 raj: eviction interaction is tricky. If we amortize, eviction_score needs to consider both current amortized balance and projected balance over next few seconds so we don't end up evicting a tenant that looks healthy now but will be net negative shortly.

 nina: proposal: eviction_score = base_priority + preempt_penalty - alpha * amortized_balance_now - beta * projected_deficit_5s + gamma * recent_cost_spike. projected_deficit_5s = max(0, outflow_rate*5 - amortized_balance_now).

 sylvie: we must be careful with monotonicity and back-and-forth eviction flips. add hysteresis: once a tenant is marked for eviction, only escalate further if score delta > hysteresis_delta, and demote only after sustained improvement window.

 tom: ops question: how do we surface this in observability? need an "amortized_balance" timeseries, "projected_deficit" gauge, plus an "eviction_cause" label for metrics to separate token-driven vs priority-driven evictions.

 nina: agreed. also suggest an "amortization_debug" sparse snapshot that includes raw events for a few tenants each minute so SRE can replay.

 elaine: cautious note: amortization could delay detection of genuine overloads, hurting p95. have a conservative default: lease_ttl=30s for small requests, 300s for long ones, and operator can tune per-pool. default peak_threshold = 1.5x normal inflight.

 raj: what about model-affinity & sku constraints? if a tenant holds amortized credit but only compatible with A100 pools, we must prevent cross-sku packing that violates model constraints. admission must always check sku_compat before applying amortized tokens.

 nina: yes: amortized balances are tagged with sku_labels; admission requires at least one matching pool with spare effective-sku-units. also keep reserved_flag to protect hard-SLA tenants (no amortization consumption).

 autoscaler-bot: canary queued: amortized-token-accounting on canary-7 at 2026-03-27T09:00Z. Dashboards: https://dashboards.redwood.internal/d/amortized-token-canary

 tom: rollout checklist: implement amortized charging + spike detector, scorer update + hysteresis, telemetry + debug snapshots, canary matrix (many-small / sudden-burst / mixed-sku), rollback if eviction_churn > 2.5x or p95 tail > 1.15x baseline in canary.

 sylvie: test idea: synthetic ramp where 200 small requests start within 2s. verify spike detector routes to absolute headroom and we don't observe silent overload.

 nina: I'll draft a short RFC patch with pseudo-code, metrics, sample dashboards, and the canary playbook. tagging @tom @elaine @raj @sylvie for review.

 elaine: thanks — please include a short operator runbook: how to toggle amortization off per-pool and how to interpret the debug snapshots.

 nina: will do. closing thread; DM me for urgent feedback.
